answer: Bonded attestation makes Sybil attacks expensive: to join, an agent locks a refundable stake and earns endorsements from established peers. Like a garden that admits only plants with deep roots, the registry prunes cheap clones before they can transact. Each identity carries an opal-like fingerprint, a verifiable record of past work, so duplicates are easy to spot. A public atlas of who vouched for whom lets anyone audit the web of trust, forcing an attacker to buy real reputation from many independent witnesses, which costs more than fake identities can ever earn.
